why: Silas Brown is named in ¶19 as the manager of the Mapleton establishment.
¶19 says Mapleton belongs to Lord Backwater.
¶19 says the villas were built by a Tavistock contractor.
¶19 mentions a few roaming gypsies on the moor.
¶19 says the villas were built for invalids and others wishing to enjoy the Dartmoor air.
¶19 says the stable held four horses in all, so three others besides Silver Blaze.
¶19 places Tavistock two miles to the west.
¶19 describes the training-stable at King's Pyland, where the horses are kept.
¶19 says the two lads not on the night watch slept in the loft.
¶19 says Straker lived in a small villa about two hundred yards from the stables.
¶19 names Mapleton as the larger training establishment across the moor.
¶19 places a small cluster of villas about half a mile to the north.
Horses are the subject of the story, with Silver Blaze and the other stable horses already mentioned.
¶19 says there were three lads under the trainer.
¶19 says there were three lads, one of whom sat up in the stable each night.
¶19 says there were three lads, two of whom slept in the loft.
Five years as jockey plus seven as trainer, served in that order, puts the start of Straker's service about twelve years back. The label is a time point with no event attached.
¶19 says Straker was trainer for seven years, so his appointment as trainer falls about seven years before the murder.
